A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching authors, title, core method, and retained experiments. Their main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite extensive rewriting and renaming.

before.justification: V1 reports original VideoQA experiments in Table 2, quantitative scene-reconstruction results in Table 3, and qualitative reconstruction and prediction examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original VideoQA results in Table 1, component analyses in Table 2, model failure cases, and a real-video reconstruction case study in Appendix E.

M1.justification: NS-4Dynamics is renamed NS-4DPhysics, retaining neural-mesh scene parsing, the Gaussian physics prior, temporal differencing and smoothing, physics-based simulation, and symbolic program execution. The expanded training description and operation inventory document the existing approach; they do not establish an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: The renamed synthetic benchmark retains factual, predictive, and counterfactual reasoning. V2 Appendix E adds a limited real-domain extension: Pascal3D+ training and a real traffic-video case study. The reported object subtype count changes from 18 to 21, although the PDFs do not establish which assets were added or whether this corrects the earlier description.

E2.justification: V2 retains the seven original VideoQA baselines and adds GPT-4o with direct and reasoning prompts, plus GPT-4o receiving predicted scene structures in Table 2. The separate reconstruction comparison against PO3D-VQA and the no-physics variant in v1 Table 3 is removed.

E3.justification: The synthetic data split, video duration, and proposed model's training budget remain unchanged. New experiments introduce eight-frame GPT-4o evaluation with direct versus step-by-step prompts and a scene-text input condition. V1's separate evaluation using translation RMSE, rotation accuracy and median error, and FLOPs is dropped.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the analyses: Table 2 tests GPT-4o reasoning over predicted 4D representations, Figure 6 adds two Video-LLM failure cases, and Appendix E adds a real-video generalization case study. The physics-prior ablation and earlier qualitative examples are retained, while the quantitative scene-reconstruction analysis from v1 Section 5.3 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The Gaussian uncertainty in the physics prior is part of the model, not uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Reported Video-LLaVA average accuracy changes from 36.04 to 38.09 and PLLaVA from 62.18 to 59.24; the reason for these updates is not explained. V2 adds GPT-4o averages of 51.59, 56.06 with reasoning, and 61.39 with 4D representations. The proposed method and no-physics variant retain 82.64 and 75.97, respectively. All quantitative reconstruction and FLOPs results from v1 Table 3 are removed, while new failure-case and real-video findings are added.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix D.1 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the contrastive training loss in Equation 7, previously only described verbally. The scene likelihood, Gaussian physics-prior formulation, and Bayes-Kalman approximation remain substantively unchanged across the appendices; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The dataset, explicit 4D representation, physics-prior method, and superior VideoQA performance remain the central contributions. V2 adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first dataset focused on language understanding of dynamic 3D-object properties, and its introduction newly claims robustness to partial occlusion and unseen poses and appearances.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the scene-text GPT-4o comparison as evidence for symbolic reasoning and attributes selected Video-LLM failures to 2D spatial confusion and inadequate motion understanding. Its limitations now explicitly exclude non-rigid or articulated objects and complex trajectories, replacing v1's emphasis on future differentiable physics and multi-frame reasoning. Appendix E also discusses missing appearance labels in the real-domain extension.

D1.justification: V2 replaces simulator placeholders with object/floor friction values of 0.2/0.4 and restitution of 0.5. It adds joint-training and momentum-update details, typed program definitions, and GPT-4o prompts, and reports released code/data instead of a planned release. These substantially improve documentation, although the earlier 7B baseline-size statement, airplane height range, and speed caps are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including CoKe, ActivityNet, Something-Something, STAR, Faster R-CNN, and counterfactually augmented video-text understanding. It removes several references, including the diffusion-based 3D-data work, and expands positioning around generative scene parsing and robustness. The main research lineage and comparison with synthetic physical-reasoning datasets remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset description, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Dataset statistics and future/counterfactual simulation receive dedicated subsections, the experimental analysis is reorganized, and the appendices are substantially restructured. Dataset/model renaming and conference formatting accompany this broader narrative revision.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figures 2 and 3, revises existing examples, adds Figures 6–11 and a detailed operation table, and separates the physics ablation into an analysis table. V1's dataset-comparison and quantitative reconstruction tables disappear. A presentation defect is introduced: main-text Equation 2 displays only '4', although the complete prior formula survives in Appendix D.2.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility by resolving simulator placeholders and documenting training, programs, and evaluation prompts. The added GPT-4o comparisons and symbolic-reasoning analysis also strengthen experimental scrutiny. These gains are tempered by removal of quantitative reconstruction evidence, omission of some settings, and the malformed main-text equation. With the core method and its benchmark scores unchanged, the net improvement is useful but limited.
